sections.h2: Where is Stafford County, Virginia, and how is it divided?
sections.html:
Stafford County lies on the Potomac and Rappahannock rivers in Northern Virginia, across the Rappahannock from the City of Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania County. It is part of the Washington metropolitan area, and it was created in 1664 from Westmoreland County and named for Staffordshire, England.

The county covers 280 square miles, of which 269 are land. Its seat is Stafford, and its largest community is Aquia Harbour. Wikipedia counts 156,927 residents in 2020 and a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 170,803.

Stafford is run by a Board of Supervisors elected from seven magisterial districts, with a county administrator managing departments. The district names are a handy way to locate a property.

  • George Washington
  • Hartwood
  • Falmouth
  • Griffis-Widewater
  • Aquia
  • Garrisonville
  • Rockhill

sections.h2: What does the 2020 census say about homes in Stafford County?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 52,793 housing units in Stafford County, and only 3.6 percent were vacant. Owners lived in 77.2 percent of occupied homes, while the rental vacancy rate was 5.2 percent.

sections.h2: How do Quantico and federal jobs shape the Stafford housing market?
sections.html:
Marine Corps Base Quantico occupies part of northern Stafford County, and the FBI Academy, the FBI National Laboratory and NCIS headquarters sit on the Stafford side of the base. Wikipedia says many residents commute north to defense and federal sites, and that many military families live in the county.

If you are selling because of a transfer or a deployment, tell your closing agent your move date early so the settlement can be scheduled around it.

  • Residents commute by I-95, U.S. 1 and the Virginia Railway Express.
  • On-post addresses at Quantico are zoned to Department of Defense schools, not the county system.
  • Wikipedia ties the county's high household incomes to its federal and defense commuters.

sections.h2: What roads and rail lines serve Stafford County?
sections.html:
Interstate 95 is the backbone, and the southern end of the I-95 Express Lanes is in Stafford County, north of Exit 133. The extension to that point was fully completed in December 2023.

U.S. 1, U.S. 17 and State Routes 3, 212 and 218 are the other major roads. The VRE commuter rail has Leeland and Brooke stations in the county, and Stafford Regional Airport is also here. A 2017 INRIX study ranked southbound I-95 from Washington to the southern tip of Stafford as the worst single traffic hotspot in the nation.

Seller takeaway: describe the drive to the VRE station and the interstate in your listing, because buyers weigh the commute heavily here.

sections.h2: What severe weather has hit Stafford County homes?
sections.html:
A tornado touched down in southern Stafford County in the early hours of May 9, 2008, and damaged about 140 suburban homes. Heavy snow has also hit: roughly 25 inches fell in December 2009 and about 19 inches in February 2010.

Buyers sometimes ask about roof age, attic insulation and tree work after storms like these. Gather any storm repair receipts and roof invoices before you list.

  • Keep proof of roof replacement or patching.
  • Note any insurance claims paid on the house.
  • Trim trees near the roofline before showings.

sections.h2: What history do Stafford County's older properties carry?
sections.html:
Stafford has colonial roots and many sites on the National Register. George Washington spent much of his childhood at Ferry Farm, and Aquia Church, built in 1757, is a National Historic Landmark. Aquia Creek sandstone from Government Island was used to build the White House and the U.S. Capitol.

The Civil War also reached the county, and more than 100,000 troops occupied it repeatedly. In 1862 about 10,000 enslaved people crossed the Rappahannock to reach Union lines, a Trail of Freedom marked on both banks. Falmouth, the town beside Fredericksburg, was the home of painter Gari Melchers, whose house Belmont is listed on the National Register. If your house is in an older area such as Falmouth or Aquia, ask the county planning office whether any local review applies.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Stafford County?
sections.html:
Stafford County Public Schools serves most of the county, with six high schools: Brooke Point, Colonial Forge, Hartwood, Mountain View, North Stafford and Stafford Senior. Areas on Marine Corps Base Quantico go to Crossroads Elementary and Quantico Middle/High School.

Germanna Community College, Strayer University and the University of Mary Washington are nearby, and private schools include Holy Cross Academy, Merit School, Fredericksburg Christian School, Saint William of York Catholic School, Fredericksburg Academy and Grace Preparatory School. Buyers confirm school zones themselves, so point them to the school division instead of promising a zone.

sections.h2: How does a Stafford County real estate assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You first ask the assessor to review the value, and if you disagree you can take the case to the Board of Equalization. The board presumes the assessor is right, and the owner must prove the home is valued above fair market value or was not assessed uniformly.

  • For a residential property with fewer than four units, you can ask in writing for the assessment records, and the assessing officer must deliver them within 15 days.
  • If the officer misses that deadline, the officer must present the records and explain the valuation method at the hearing before you speak.
  • Sales through December 31 before the assessment date may be used, and later studies cannot.
  • The board may raise or lower values, with or without a specific complaint.

Separately, errors made by the assessor or factual errors made during a general reassessment can be corrected by application within three years of the end of the tax year or one year of the assessment, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What happens to Stafford County property tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax is settled from the sale proceeds, because the county's tax lien ranks ahead of other liens until the treasurer is paid. Penalty and interest count as part of the tax owed.

Virginia ruleWhat it means for a Stafford seller
Tax lienTaxes, penalties and interest are paid from sale proceeds
Current-year shareProrated by the sale contract between seller and buyer
Grantor tax50 cents per $500 of value, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to pay
Delinquent tax salePossible after a set number of years unpaid, with 30 days' notice first
Installment planUp to 72 months if the treasurer agrees

faqs.q: Who assesses and who collects property tax in Stafford County?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses property, and the Treasurer collects the tax. Both are elected county officers. Call them for your parcel's current balance and deadlines.

faqs.q: Is Stafford County part of Northern Virginia?
faqs.a: Yes. Stafford County is in the Washington metropolitan area and is generally counted in Northern Virginia, about 25 miles south of Washington, D.C. by Wikipedia's account.

faqs.q: What tax rules apply if I inherit a house in Stafford County?
faqs.a: Unpaid taxes stay as a lien on the house until paid. Virginia law also lets heirs who claim ownership by will or intestacy ask the treasurer to pause a tax sale, and installment plans can run up to 72 months.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stafford County house that I owe tax on?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is paid from the proceeds at closing, and the treasurer releases the lien afterward. If the debt is larger than the sale price, you will need to talk to the treasurer and your closing agent first.

faqs.q: How big is Stafford County compared with its neighbors?
faqs.a: Stafford covers 280 square miles, with 269 of them land. It borders Prince William, Fauquier, Culpeper, Caroline, King George and Spotsylvania counties, the City of Fredericksburg, and Charles County, Maryland, across the Potomac.

faqs.q: Where do Stafford County deeds get recorded?
faqs.a: With the Stafford County Clerk of the Circuit Court. The deed must state the sale price on its first page, and the grantor tax is collected when it is recorded.
